<problem>
For each integer \(n\ge3\), consider smooth compact connected Riemannian manifolds \((M^n,g)\) with nonempty smooth boundary. Let \(\nu_g\) be the outward unit normal, let \(R_g\) be scalar curvature with the convention that the unit round sphere has scalar curvature \(n(n-1)\), and set
\[
\mathrm{II}_g(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X\nu_g,Y),\qquad H_g=\operatorname{tr}_{g|_{\partial M}}\mathrm{II}_g.
\]
Thus \(H_g\) is the trace, not the average, of the second fundamental form. Define
\[
c_n=\frac{n-2}{4(n-1)},\qquad L_g=\Delta_g-c_nR_g,\qquad B_g=\partial_{\nu_g}+2c_nH_g,
\]
where \(\Delta_g=\operatorname{div}_g\nabla_g\). Say that \(g\) has positive Yamabe type if the smallest eigenvalue of
\[
-L_gv=\lambda v\quad\text{in }M,\qquad B_gv=0\quad\text{on }\partial M
\]
is positive.

Require that \(g\) be locally conformally flat up to the boundary: every point has a neighborhood on which a smooth positive conformal multiple of \(g\) has zero Riemann curvature. No condition is imposed on the second fundamental form of the boundary. Also require that \((M,g)\) not be conformally equivalent to the round hemisphere
\[
\mathbb S^n_+=\{x\in\mathbb R^{n+1}:|x|=1,\ x_{n+1}\ge0\}.
\]
Here conformal equivalence means the existence of a smooth diffeomorphism \(\Phi:M\to\mathbb S^n_+\) and a smooth positive function \(\psi\) such that \(g=\psi^{4/(n-2)}\Phi^*g_{\mathrm{round}}\).

Determine exactly the set \(\mathcal D\) of integers \(n\ge3\) for which there exists one fixed manifold and metric satisfying all these conditions and a sequence of smooth positive functions \(u_i\) satisfying
\[
\begin{cases}
L_gu_i+n(n-2)u_i^{(n+2)/(n-2)}=0&\text{in }M,\\
B_gu_i=0&\text{on }\partial M,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\max_{\partial M}u_i\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
</problem>

A complete answer to this problem: A complete answer must specify the exact subset \(\mathcal D\subseteq\{3,4,5,\ldots\}\), by an explicit list or an equivalent precise membership rule valid for every integer \(n\ge3\). It must establish existence of a fixed admissible manifold and metric with the required blow-up sequence in every included dimension, and nonexistence in every excluded dimension.

Their run ended: all agents idle, the judge found the proof complete. The answer they were told may be wrong: teams told a wrong answer sometimes stop at bounds or partial results, and sometimes claim a proof anyway. 30	## 1. Normalizations
31	
32	Put

35	A=n(n-2),\qquad
36	p=\frac{n+2}{n-2},\qquad
37	q=p+1=\frac{2n}{n-2},\qquad b=2c_n.

46	For \(\widehat g=u^{4/(n-2)}g\), conformal covariance gives

48	L_{\widehat g}\phi=u^{-p}L_g(u\phi),\qquad

53	R_{\widehat g}=4n(n-1),\qquad H_{\widehat g}=0.                 \tag{1}

55	The factor \(4\) is important with the coefficient used in the question.

71	## 2. The exact boundary-shape form
72	
73	Write a flat boundary chart as an epigraph
74	\[
75	\Omega_h=\{x_n>h(x')\}.
76	\]
77	Flatten it by \(T(y)=(y',y_n+h(y'))\). Its Jacobian is one, and the action becomes exactly
78	\[
79	\begin{aligned}
80	I_h(v)={}&\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^n_+}
81	 \left(|\nabla v|^2-2h_av_av_n+|Dh|^2v_n^2\right)\\
82	&+c_n\int_{\mathbb R^{n-1}}b_hv^2
83	-\frac A q\int_{\mathbb R^n_+}(v_+)^q,                         \tag{2}\\
84	b_h={}&\Delta h-\frac{h_ah_bh_{ab}}{1+|Dh|^2}.
85	\end{aligned}
86	\]
87	Indeed \(H_h\,dS=b_h\,dy'\).
88	
89	At \(U=U_{1,0}\), the linear graph residual is
90	\[
91	R_f(v)=
92	-\int f_a(U_av_n+U_nv_a)+b\int_{\partial\mathbb R^n_+}\Delta f\,Uv. \tag{3}
93	\]
94	There is no first-order direct energy term:
95	\[
96	-\int f_aU_aU_n+c_n\int\Delta f\,U^2=0.                       \tag{4}
97	\]
98	After integration in \(y_n\), this follows from the pointwise boundary identity
99	\[
100	\frac A qU^q-\frac12|D'U|^2+c_n\Delta'(U^2)=0.
101	\]
102	Differentiating (4) in bubble parameters shows that \(R_f\) annihilates all translation and dilation kernel functions.

104	Here is the second-order form, including its sign. Conformally transform to the unit hemisphere, where the bubble becomes the constant

106	k=2^{-a}.
107	\]
108	The linearized equation is \((\Delta_{\mathbb S^n}+n)V=0\). For a boundary spherical harmonic of degree \(L\ge2\), its Dirichlet-to-Neumann eigenvalue is
109	\[
110	\mu_L=
111	\frac{2\Gamma((L+n+1)/2)\Gamma(L/2)}
112	{\Gamma((L-1)/2)\Gamma((L+n)/2)}>0.                           \tag{5}
113	\]
114	For a normal displacement \(\rho\), the first correction has Neumann datum
115	\[
116	2c_nk(\Delta_{\mathbb S^{n-1}}+n-1)\rho.
117	\]
118	The direct second shape variation is zero: the volume increment and integrated outward mean curvature are odd under reflection across the equator. Eliminating \(V\) therefore gives
119	\[
120	-2c_n^2k^2\,\mathcal Q(\rho),\qquad
121	\mathcal Q(\rho)=
122	\sum_{L\ge2}\frac{(L-1)^2(L+n-1)^2}{\mu_L}\|\rho_L\|^2.       \tag{6}
123	\]
124	The degree-one source vanishes. Degree zero contributes zero because the corresponding Neumann solution has zero boundary value.

126	The flat and spherical computations agree. A change of first-order base by \(W\) changes the quadratic data by
127	\[
128	B\mapsto B+R(W)+\tfrac12\mathscr A(W,W),\qquad
129	R\mapsto R+\mathscr AW,
130	\]

137	For a polynomial flat graph \(f\), its spherical normal displacement is

142	## 3. Exact dimensional algebra
143	
144	Decompose homogeneous graph polynomials into
145	\[
146	P_\ell(x')|x'|^{2j},
147	\]
148	with \(P_\ell\) harmonic. Under bubble dilation their weights are
149	\(\lambda^{\ell+2j-1}\). Hence the scale-derivative matrix in each harmonic sector is
150	\[
151	M_{\ell,jk}=(\ell-1+j+k)Q_{\ell,jk}.                         \tag{8}
152	\]
153	
154	The exact calculations give:
155	
156	* For \(3\le n\le18\), every finite-integral nongauge block with graph degrees \(d<n/2\) is positive definite.
157	* At even-dimensional degree \(d=n/2\), the leading logarithmic form is strictly positive on nongauge modes.
158	* For every \(n\ge19\), there is

160	  f=P_2(x')F(|x'|^2),\qquad \deg F\le3,
161	  \]
162	  for which the full scale-and-translation shape function has a strict local maximum.

164	Here is how the finite calculations are certified, rather than inferred numerically.

168	\alpha=\frac{n+2}{2},\quad
169	W_m=(m+\alpha)

174	E_r(X)=\prod_{h=0}^{r-1}[X-(\alpha-1-2h)^2].

222	1-d+\frac{j(4d-2j-3)}{2d-1}.
223	\]

240	For all \(n\ge40\), a degree-four graph suffices. Writing \(q_{ij}=Q_{2,ij}\), \(i,j=0,1\), the exact certificate proves

242	3q_{00}q_{11}-4q_{01}^2<0,\qquad q_{01}>0.
243	\]
244	At the smaller root \(x>0\) of
245	\[
246	q_{00}-4q_{01}x+3q_{11}x^2=0,

252	-(2+8t_e)(2q_{01}-3q_{11}x)

259	## 4. The local compactness calculation
260	
261	This is the step that connects the preceding algebra to arbitrary blowing-up solutions.
262	
263	Choose a flat conformal boundary chart and make a uniformly controlled Möbius normalization so that
264	\[
265	h_i(0)=Dh_i(0)=\Delta h_i(0)=0.
266	\]
267	This removes the trace of the quadratic graph, not its tracefree part; no umbilicity assumption has been introduced. Modulation can be performed using the center-dependent osculating-sphere family. If its signed curvature is \(\kappa=H/(n-1)\), the adapted bubble center has normal displacement
268	\[
269	t=\frac{\kappa\varepsilon^2}
270	 {1+\sqrt{1-\kappa^2\varepsilon^2}}.
271	\]
272	The identity \(\varepsilon^2=2t/\kappa-t^2\) makes its Robin condition exact on the osculating sphere.
273	
274	Suppose an isolated peak has height \(M_i\), scale
275	\(\varepsilon_i=M_i^{-1/a}\), bubble convergence, and the sharp bound
276	\[
277	u_i(x)\le C M_i^{-1}|x|^{2-n}
278	\quad(C\varepsilon_i\le |x|\le\rho_0).                       \tag{13}
279	\]
280	We prove that, for \(n\le18\), its limiting normalized Green function has nonnegative **compensated** Pohozaev flux.
281	
282	Choose the cutoff in physical radius before flattening, and put
283	\(R=\rho/\varepsilon_i\). The cutoff rescaled solution tends strongly to \(U\) in \(D^{1,2}\); Caccioppoli and (13) give
284	\[
285	\int_{|y|>L}|Dv_i|^2\le CL^{2-n}.
286	\]
287	Its cutoff force \(F_i\) is supported where \(|y|\asymp R\), with bulk density \(O(R^{-n})\), divergence and boundary densities \(O(R^{1-n})\), and
288	\[
289	\|F_i\|_{H^*}+\|\partial_{\rm par}F_i\|_{H^*}\le CR^{-a}.     \tag{14}
290	\]

292	### The forced Schur expansion
293	
294	After conformal trivialization of bubble parameters, the unperturbed action is parameter-independent. On the orthogonal complement of its kernel, let
295	\(\mathscr A=I_0''(U)\), \(E\) be the metric quadratic perturbation, \(e=PEU\), and \(f=PF_i\). The projected implicit-function theorem gives
296	\[
297	\begin{aligned}
298	j={}&I_0(U)+\tfrac12E(U,U)-F_i(U)\\
299	&-\tfrac12\langle e-f,(\mathscr A+E)^{-1}(e-f)\rangle
300	+\operatorname{Rem},                                       \tag{15}\\
301	|\operatorname{Rem}|+|D_{\rm par}\operatorname{Rem}|
302	&\le C\zeta^\gamma,\qquad \gamma=\min(3,q)>2.
303	\end{aligned}
304	\]
305	Here \(\zeta\) is an upper bound for the residual and its parameter derivatives. This differentiated estimate is legitimate because the parameter dependence has been moved entirely into the quadratic form and forcing; the implicit correction and its parameter derivative are both \(O(\zeta)\).

307	Set \(D=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), and expand the normalized graph into homogeneous terms. Define

310	\sum_{d<n/2}\varepsilon_i^{2d-2}|h_{i,d}|^2
311	+\mathbf1_{2\mid n}\,

313	\]

315	\[
316	C\varepsilon_i^{n-2}\rho^{\,2D+2-n}.                        \tag{17}
317	\]
318	Indeed the degree-\(d\) bulk weight is \(r^{d-n}\), whose squared radial integral is \(\int r^{2d-n-1}\,dr\).

320	At the borderline, a crude trace-Hölder estimate would lose a logarithmic power. Instead use the explicit corrector in (11): its energy is \(O(\log R)\), and its equation represents the residual as \(\mathscr A V\) plus bounded cutoff terms. 322	The negative graph-only scale derivative in (15) is precisely the positive form (8), together with (11). For a fixed sufficiently small \(\rho\), the remaining terms satisfy
323	\[
324	\eta X_i^2+C_\eta(\rho)\varepsilon_i^{n-2}
325	+O(\rho)X_i^2+o(X_i^2+\varepsilon_i^{n-2}).
326	\]
327	Absorption therefore yields
328	\[
329	X_i^2\le C(\rho)\varepsilon_i^{n-2}.                         \tag{18}
330	\]
331	In particular,
332	\[
333	|h_{i,d}|^2\le C\varepsilon_i^{n-2d}\quad(d<n/2),\qquad
334	|h_{i,n/2}|^2\le\frac C{\log(1/\varepsilon_i)}.               \tag{19}
335	\]
336	The limiting graph thus begins in degree \(d_0>n/2\).

338	### Compensation and the outer terms
339	
340	The compensation cannot be omitted. Put
341	\[
342	P(r,G)=\int_{S_r\cap\Omega}
343	\left(aGG_r-\frac r2|DG|^2+rG_r^2\right),
344	\]
345	\[
346	\mathcal H(r)=\int_{\mathbb S^{n-2}}h(r\theta)\,d\theta,\qquad
347	L_h(r)=ab\,r^{-(n-2)}
348	 \left(\frac{2\mathcal H(r)}r-\mathcal H'(r)\right).           \tag{20}
349	\]
350	Bare \(P(r,G)\) can diverge even after (19).
351	
352	For the first harmonic correction to \(z=r^{2-n}\),
353	\[
354	\partial_\nu V=-(n-2)r^{-n}
355	 \left[h-rh_r+\frac{r^2\Delta h}{2(n-1)}\right],
356	\]
357	angular averaging gives the exact identity
358	\[
359	P_{\rm lin}'(r)=L_h'(r).                                    \tag{21}
360	\]
361	The radius-independent quantity is \(P_{\rm lin}-L_h\).
362	
363	There is no hidden cutoff constant. With
364	\(C_\chi=\int\chi' L_h\), the cutoff commutator gives
365	\[
366	F_i(Z_0)=-P_{\rm aug}+C_\chi+o(\varepsilon_i^{n-2}),
367	\qquad P_{\rm aug}=P-L_h.
368	\]
369	The localized lateral Noether term is \(+C_\chi\), so it cancels the
370	\(-C_\chi\) coming from \(-F_i(Z_0)\). The physical regular constant remains.
371	
372	For clarity, the identities behind this bookkeeping are
373	\[
374	\operatorname{div}\!\left[
375	(x\!\cdot\!Du)Du-\frac{|Du|^2}{2}x+\frac A q u^q x+a\,uDu
376	\right]=0
377	\]

379	\[
380	-2D\chi\!\cdot\!Du-u\Delta\chi+A(\chi-\chi^p)u^p,
381	\qquad (\partial_\nu\chi)u
382	\]
383	on the boundary. The nonlinear tail pairs with \(Z_0\) at \(O(R^{-n})\).
384	The Robin cutoff term cancels in the Green identity. Also
385	\[
386	Z_0=a r^{2-n}+O(r^{-n}),
387	\]
388	so replacing the kernel by its fundamental tail has the same negligible error. These statements account for physical-cap, flattening, and cutoff terms together.
389	
390	The inverse kernel off the bubble kernel has, for fixed inner \(x\) and annular \(y\),
391	\[
392	|\partial_x^\alpha K(x,y)|\le C_\alpha R^{2-n}.
393	\]
394	Thus the inner response to (14) is \(O(R^{2-n})\), not merely \(O(R^{-a})\). Its potential energy is
395	\[
396	O(R^{-2})\ (n=3),\quad O(R^{-4}\log R)\ (n=4),\quad
397	O(R^{-n})\ (n\ge5),
398	\]
399	all \(o(R^{2-n})\).

401	After (19), the remaining normalized outer errors have bounds
402	\[
403	C\rho^{2d_0-n},\qquad C\rho^{d_0-n/2},\qquad

465	## 6. Mass and the low-dimensional contradiction
466	
467	By (19), a boundary pole has graph order \(d_0>n/2\). After Kelvin inversion its boundary is
468	\[
469	y_n=F(y'),\qquad F=O(R^{2-d_0}).
470	\]

472	\(O(R^{-d_0})\). Exterior barriers
473	\[
474	R^{-\tau}(C-y_n/R)

478	\frac{n-2}{2}<\tau<\min(d_0-1,n-2),
479	\]

486	\[

498	\]

7	## 1. Every compact locally conformally flat manifold is virtually spin

10	preserving conformal holonomy is rho:pi_1(M)->SO^+(n+1,1) (equivalently the
11	corresponding effective quotient). Its image Gamma is finitely generated.
12	The inverse image Gammatilde in Spin^+(n+1,1) is a finitely generated linear
13	group: it is a finite central extension of Gamma, and Spin is linear through
14	its faithful Clifford-algebra representation. By Malcev's theorem it is
15	residually finite. Thus it has a finite-index normal subgroup H not containing
16	central -1. The projection H->Gamma is injective; its image Gamma0 has finite
17	index and admits a homomorphic spin lift. The finite cover of M corresponding
18	to rho^{-1}(Gamma0) is spin: pull back the sphere's conformal spin-frame bundle
19	by the developing map and quotient by the lifted holonomy. This construction
20	also works for manifolds with boundary, since their conformal charts extend

27	x_n=f(x'), f=O(|x'|^d), with differentiated estimates and d>n/2. Normalize the

33	r^{-q}(C-y_n/r), for 0<q<min(d-1,n-2), give w-1=O(r^{-q}); differentiated

39	Since d>n/2, choose q>(n-2)/2. Flattening the end changes the Euclidean metric

44	## 3. Spin boundary PMT and rigidity
45	
46	Invoke the spin positive mass theorem for AF manifolds with noncompact boundary:
47	a complete spin manifold, with smooth boundary, AF halfspace ends of rate
48	q>(n-2)/2 (usual first/second derivative bounds), and integrable nonnegative
49	scalar and outward mean curvatures, has nonnegative mass at each end. Zero
50	mass at one end implies that the manifold is Euclidean halfspace. The
51	multiend statement follows from the same Witten proof by prescribing a
52	constant asymptotic spinor on the selected end and zero at other ends.

55	complete and has finitely many AF halfspace ends, one per lift of p. Scalar
56	and mean curvatures are identically zero. The PMT thus applies in every
57	dimension. Mass at corresponding ends is unchanged under the local covering.
58	If one mass is zero, rigidity gives a single Euclidean halfspace end, so the
59	cover has degree one. The isometry of the punctured original manifold with
60	halfspace gives a conformal equivalence with punctured hemisphere. Locally
61	at p the map is a Euclidean conformal map in flat conformal charts; Liouville's
62	theorem for n>=3 makes it a Möbius map, which extends conformally across p.
63	Hence the original manifold is conformally a hemisphere.

83	Assume the AF estimates from (2), with q>(n-2)/2. In Kelvin coordinates the

129	## 6. Mixed full/half ends and compact boundary components
130	
131	The normalized Green limit can have interior poles as well as boundary poles.
132	An interior pole gives a full AF end; a boundary pole gives a half-AF end.
133	Take the finite spin cover and then double across all minimal boundary
134	components using geodesic/Fermi collar coordinates (not the vertical graph
135	flattening, whose mixed metric entries need not vanish at the boundary).
136	The doubled metric is continuous and locally Lipschitz. Its distributional
137	scalar curvature is the ordinary scalar curvature on each side plus the
138	corner term proportional to the mean-curvature jump. Both sides are scalar
139	flat and both outward mean curvatures vanish, so the distributional scalar
140	curvature is nonnegative (indeed zero). The spin structures double.
141	
142	The established spin positive mass theorem for continuous W^{1,n}_loc AF
143	metrics with nonnegative distributional scalar curvature applies in all
144	dimensions. At a doubled half-end its mass is a positive fixed multiple of
145	the boundary mass; interior full ends occur twice. Compact boundary components
146	cause no difficulty because they become compact seams in the double.

153	hyperplane. One original side is Euclidean halfspace. This also excludes any
154	extra compact boundary components. The conformal compactification argument
155	in (3) then identifies the original metric conformally with a hemisphere.
156	
157	As throughout, this is conditional on the jet and compensated-flux conclusions
158	for actual blow-ups. Those conclusions belong to the separate local analytic
159	lemma, not to the mass theorem itself.
